cover.headline: The Suven-Cohance merger has not worked yet: EPS fell from ₹12.7 to a Q1 loss and the stock 61% since the merger; on our rule 43.5x Sep-28E EPS gives {{dcf.tp|inr}}, SELL
cover.lead: Cohance Lifesciences is Advent International's merger of Suven Pharmaceuticals (a high-margin contract manufacturer for innovator drug companies) with Cohance (niche APIs and formulations), effective 1-May-2025, plus two bolt-ons: 56% of NJ Bio (US antibody-drug-conjugate services) and 67.5% of Sapala (oligonucleotide building blocks). Since the merger two big CDMO molecules destocked, a US FDA Warning Letter hit the Nacharam formulations plant, NJ Bio's losses grew and four senior leaders left; FY26 revenue fell 13%, and Q1FY27 had a 0.3% EBITDA margin and a loss. Ex-Cipla CEO Umang Vohra took charge in May-2026 and guides recovery from H2FY27. We forecast EPS of ₹3.2 / 5.9 / 8.5 for FY27-29E, 14-23% below BOBCAPS. We value on **P/E**, the street's method. Both forward years since the merger are trough years under our rule, so the multiple comes from the listed share's history since Apr-2021 (40.4x, trough years left out) × the pharma sector's +8.2%: **43.5x Sep-28E EPS of ₹7.2 = {{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}): we initiate with SELL**. Cross-checks: EV/EBITDA ₹400; DCF ₹129. Bull {{scen.bull.tp|inr}}; bear {{scen.bear.tp|inr}}.

arguments.p: Attributable EPS ₹12.68 (FY25, merged) → ₹4.68 (FY26) → −₹0.63 in Q1FY27. The cost base (~₹300 cr a quarter) did not fall with revenue. Without NJ Bio's US partners absorbing 44% of its losses, the Q1 loss would have been ₹45 cr, not ₹24 cr.

arguments.h: A recovery is likely, its size is not
arguments.p: A restocking order for one destocked molecule (deliveries Q4FY27-FY28), two newly commercial molecules, 10 Phase III molecules, Sapala up 2.5x and Nacharam back to supplying the US. But the second molecule, NJ Bio (₹33 cr EBITDA loss in Q1) and agrochemicals (a qualification year) are open; the US$1 bn FY30 target is now an "aspiration".

Advent controls 57.5%, sold 8.9% at ~₹906 in Sep-2025 to repay holdco debt and has pledged 54% of the company for a US$285 mn loan. Executive chairman, MD, CEO and CFO all changed in eleven months; a Form 483 (five observations) at the Pashamylaram CDMO site in Aug-2026.

arguments.h: The price already pays for the recovery
arguments.p: ₹444 is 75.5x our FY28E and ~62x Sep-28E EPS. Pre-merger Suven traded at 30-45x forward; BOBCAPS uses 40x. The DCF supports ~₹129 and needs ~28% revenue growth for 15 years to reach the price. Street median target ₹365.

catalysts: Q2FY27 results (due by mid-November 2026): management guides better than Q1; watch the CDMO deliveries moved from Q1, the ADC payload order and NJ Bio losses.
Umang Vohra's strategy update and a view on the US$1 bn FY30 aspiration, promised by December 2026; a new CFO (Himanshu Agarwal left on 13-Sep-2026).
US FDA: response to the Pashamylaram Form 483 (five observations); Nacharam CAPA audit-ready by end-FY27.
Restocking: deliveries for the first destocked molecule from Q4FY27; any order for the second.
Advent: the Sep-2025 lock-up has expired; any further block sale or change to the holdco pledge.

sections.title: What Cohance does: makes molecules for drug companies (Pharma CDMO, 39%), sells niche APIs and formulations (API+, 48%) and makes agro and performance chemicals (13%)

blocks.p: Cohance is a contract manufacturer and API maker for the pharmaceutical industry. **Pharma CDMO** (contract development and manufacturing; 39% of FY26 revenue) makes intermediates and active ingredients to an innovator's recipe, mostly for drugs still under patent: Suven's old business, built on 30-year relationships with large drug companies (the top 20 innovators give over 85% of small-molecule revenue). It also includes two newer platforms: payloads and linkers for antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs, "guided missile" cancer drugs) made in Vizag and the US bioconjugation services of **NJ Bio** (56% owned), and building blocks for oligonucleotide drugs from **Sapala** (67.5% owned). **API+** (48%) is Cohance's old business: niche, low-volume generic APIs (central nervous system drugs, controlled substances; top-three global position in 8 of its top 10 molecules), pellets and finished formulations sold to generic companies and some innovators. **Specialty Chemicals** (13%) makes agrochemical intermediates and active ingredients for an anchor global innovator and performance materials (photochromic dyes for lenses, OLED materials).

About half of revenue is now API+, a good niche-API business but a lower-margin one than innovator CDMO; the high-value CDMO book is concentrated in a few molecules; and the two "new modality" platforms are small (NJ Bio and Sapala ~10% of revenue) and one of them loses money.

sections.title: History: Advent bought Suven (2023), built Cohance alongside, merged them (May-2025), bought two bolt-ons and sold 8.9% at ₹906

blocks.p: Suven Pharmaceuticals was demerged from Suven Life Sciences in 2020 and run by the Jasti family. Advent International bought 50.1% in 2023 (~₹6,313 cr agreed in Dec-2022) with a plan to merge it with **Cohance Lifesciences**, an API, formulations and CDMO platform Advent had assembled from acquisitions (AR FY26 lists land held in the names of RA Chem Pharma, Avra Laboratories and Inventis Drug Delivery Systems). The board approved the merger on 29-Feb-2024; the NCLT sanctioned it on 27-Mar-2025 and it became effective on **1-May-2025**: Suven issued **12,80,02,184 new shares at 11 Suven shares for every 295 Cohance shares** (record date 9-May-2025), taking the share count from 25.46 cr to 38.26 cr and Advent's stake to 66.41%; the merged company took the Cohance name. Because both companies were under Advent's control, the merger was booked by **pooling of interests**: FY25 was restated as if they had always been one and no assets were marked up, so there is no large amortisation of merger intangibles in the numbers. Before the merger each side bought a bolt-on: Cohance bought 67.5% of Sapala for ₹258 cr (Jul-2024) and Suven 56% of NJ Bio for ₹548 cr (Dec-2024), both with obligations to buy the rest (₹696 cr liability at Mar-26).

blocks.callout: **So what:** for a Suven shareholder the merger looked accretive in FY25 (EPS ₹12.68 merged vs ₹10.40 for Suven alone). It brought scale and a second leg (API+), and diluted Suven's margin (39% in FY24 alone vs 31% merged in FY25). The bolt-ons cost ~₹806 cr for majority stakes plus ₹696 cr owed for the rest; together they earned ₹238 cr of revenue and lost ₹66 cr in FY26.

sections.title: Why the stock fell 61% since the merger: two guidance cuts, a block sale, a Warning Letter and leadership churn, then a bounce on a new chief

blocks.p: On the merger's effective date the stock closed the week at ₹1,136 (2-May-2025): ~90x the merged FY25 EPS reported later that month, a price that leaned on the US$1 bn revenue / mid-30s-margin FY30 target. Each step since took the earnings and the multiple down together. **Aug-2025**: a weak Q1FY26. **18-Sep-2025**: Advent's Jusmiral Holdings sold 8.92% at ~₹906 to repay holdco debt (210-day lock-up). **Oct-Nov 2025**: the MD resigned and Q2FY26 cut FY26 revenue guidance to flat and margins to the high-20s (stock −27% in 11 sessions). **Feb-2026**: FY26 revenue guidance cut again to an early-to-mid double-digit decline, a US FDA Warning Letter at Nacharam, the CEO left: the stock touched ~₹280 in Mar-2026 (−75% from the merger). **27-Apr-2026**: Umang Vohra, who ran Cipla for a decade, was named Executive Chairman and Group CEO; the stock hit a 20% upper circuit and rose 43% in two days. **May and Aug-2026**: Q4FY26 and Q1FY27 were as weak as guided (Q1 loss) and the stock has held at ₹420-460 since: the market is paying for Vohra and a FY28 recovery, not for current earnings.

sections.title: Industry: CDMO grows ~7% a year, ADC and oligonucleotide services ~11-15%; India gains from China de-risking, slowly

blocks.p: Global pharma CDMO market ~US$197.4 bn in 2025, projected ~US$368.7 bn by 2034 (7.15% CAGR) (AR FY26 MD&A, citing industry reports). 22 ADCs approved globally by May-2026 (14 by the US FDA); ADC sales ~US$16.1 bn in 2025 (Enhertu US$5.0 bn, Padcev US$3.0 bn, Adcetris US$1.6 bn); ADC contract manufacturing ~US$8.9 bn (2024) to ~US$16.5 bn (2030), ~10.9% a year; bioconjugation CDMO ~US$2.2 bn (2025) to ~US$4.4 bn (2030), ~15% a year (AR FY26 MD&A). Oligonucleotide CDMO ~US$0.91 bn (2024) to ~US$3.16 bn (2033), ~15% a year (AR FY26 MD&A); company deck: oligo market US$1 bn (FY24) to US$4 bn (FY29E). US de-risking from Chinese suppliers (Department of Defense list naming Chinese CDMOs; BIOSECURE-type legislation) is lifting late-stage RFQs to Indian CDMOs, but customers already have one or two sources, so conversion is slow (Cohance CDMO CEO, q1call). API+ sits in the slower generic API market (Global API market ~US$270.5 bn in 2025 to ~US$419 bn by 2033), and specialty chemicals in a ~3.5%-growth market with agrochemicals in a global downturn.

sections.title: Tailwind test: Indian CDMO peers are growing; Cohance is not, yet. The tailwind reaches it with a lag and through a few molecules

blocks.p: Indian CDMOs had a strong FY26: on Screener, Neuland grew revenue 37%, Acutaas 33%, Sai Life 29%, Laurus 23%, Anthem 15% and Divi's 13%, helped by innovators adding non-Chinese suppliers. Cohance's revenue fell 13%. Its new chairman said it plainly: "some of our peers may have actually moved faster than Cohance", partly because of leadership churn, and its anchor customers "did not necessarily increase the width of their business with us in the past 2 to 3 years". The tailwind is real for Cohance too (RFQs have doubled since FY23; late-stage inquiries from large pharma and Western CDMOs are rising) but conversion takes years because customers already have one or two qualified sources. Our forecasts assume it shows up from FY28 (small-molecule CDMO +25%), not in FY27.

blocks.callout: **Verdict:** the sector tailwind reaches Cohance weakly and late. Unlike Sai Life or Anthem, which are compounding broad customer books, Cohance's CDMO revenue swings with a handful of molecules (two destocked at once). Q1FY27 small-molecule CDMO revenue was only ~₹62 cr against ~₹163 cr a quarter in FY26.

sections.title: Small-molecule CDMO: Suven's engine stalled when two big molecules destocked; one is restocking, two new ones are commercial, 10 sit in Phase III

blocks.p: This is the old Suven business: intermediates and APIs for innovator drugs, made under long contracts with the top 20 innovators (>85% of small-molecule revenue). It is lumpy because a few molecules matter a lot. In FY26 two large commercial molecules were **destocked** (customers ran down their inventories), costing ~₹260 cr of revenue, and two older molecules are past patent expiry (already declining). Pharma CDMO revenue fell from ₹1,128 cr to ₹889 cr, and to ₹124.8 cr in Q1FY27 (−39%); stripping out NJ Bio and Sapala, small-molecule revenue was only ~₹62 cr in Q1 against ~₹163 cr a quarter in FY26. The pipeline is the case for recovery: two molecules moved into commercial supply (six intermediates, deliveries q2-q3fy27); two more expected in 12-15 months, one already us fda approved; a **restocking order** has been received for one destocked molecule with deliveries in Q4FY27 and FY28; the second is still "in discussion"; there are 10 molecules in Phase III (management expects more than half to be approved) and 140+ active projects. Commercial work was 57% of Q1FY27 standalone CDMO revenue (over 70% in FY26). Customer concentration is not disclosed.

The bull case needs the second molecule back and faster Phase III conversion; the bear case is that the reloads are smaller than the destocking.

sections.title: ADC and oligonucleotides: NJ Bio cost ₹548 cr for 56% and loses ~₹50 cr a quarter; Sapala cost ₹258 cr for 67.5% and is growing 2.5x

blocks.p: These are the platforms that were meant to make Cohance a "technology-driven CDMO" (niche technologies were 15-16% of revenue). **ADC**: in India Cohance makes payloads (the toxic drug) and linkers in Vizag, with two commercial payload supplies to large innovators, three payload DMFs filed in FY26 and MMAE and exatecan added; a customised payload order is due in Q2FY27. **NJ Bio** (Princeton, New Jersey; 56% bought on 20-Dec-2024 for ₹548 cr, goodwill ₹419 cr; the other 44% can be put to Cohance) does research and clinical-scale bioconjugation: revenue ₹188 cr and a loss of ₹66 cr in FY26, then revenue of ₹35.0 cr and an EBITDA loss of ₹32.8 cr in Q1FY27 alone, after biotech funding dried up and full-time-equivalent (FTE) research contracts were lost. Management's goal is to make its cost "commensurate" with revenue; profitability is "a medium-term objective". **Oligonucleotides**: **Sapala** (Hyderabad; 67.5% bought on 11-Jul-2024 for ₹258 cr) makes amidites and modified nucleosides, the building blocks of antisense and siRNA drugs: FY26 revenue ₹49.7 cr (a small loss after acquisition accounting), Q1FY27 ₹27.4 cr (2.5x) at a strong margin, with orders in hand and a new amidites plant. Founder Dr P.Y. Reddy now leads the combined nucleic-acid business, with a path to 100% ownership by FY30.

sections.title: API+: the stable half, hurt by a US FDA Warning Letter at Nacharam; niche APIs with top-3 global positions; guided to double-digit growth from FY28

blocks.p: API+ (₹1,088 cr, 48% of FY26 revenue) is Cohance's legacy business: low-to-mid-volume generic APIs where it has built cost leadership through backward integration (8 of its top 10 molecules hold top-three global positions; the top 15 products are about half of API revenue), pellets and finished formulations. About two-thirds of revenue is with innovators or large generic companies. FY26 revenue fell 8%: shipment delays, softer demand in some mature products and the **Nacharam formulations plant**, which received an OAI and then a **US FDA Warning Letter (Feb-2026)**, was voluntarily shut for remediation and cost ~₹61 cr of revenue; supplies have resumed (US supplies restarted) and the site should be "audit-ready" by end-FY27. Q1FY27 revenue fell 10% on order timing and a customer-site event, with prices passed through. Management targets seven API filings in FY27 (nine in FY26) and ~10 formulation launches, and sees "steady", double-digit growth from FY28.

blocks.callout: **Our view:** API+ is the bedrock: we forecast +3% / +11% / +10% for FY27-29E. It is a good niche-generic business, but not innovator CDMO economics: BOBCAPS calls API+ at ~60% of Q1 sales "an industry-low margin for a CDMO company" and uses that to justify a 40x multiple.

sections.title: Specialty chemicals: agrochemicals in a downturn and a "qualification year"; photochromic stable, OLED in transition

blocks.p: Specialty Chemicals (₹291 cr, 13%) makes agrochemical intermediates and active ingredients, mostly for one anchor global innovator, and performance materials (photochromic dyes for spectacle lenses, OLED and deuterated materials, early semiconductor chemistry). Revenue fell 2% in FY26 on Chinese generic pricing in agro and fell 35% in Q1FY27 as agro shipments shifted to H2. Management calls FY27 "a year of qualification" (a key active ingredient entered registration; first campaigns with two Japanese innovators) and sees double-digit growth from FY28. The business is being "revamped" with new capacity, governance and an innovator-led portfolio.

blocks.callout: **Our view:** −9% / +12% / +12% for FY27-29E. Too small to move the valuation; a source of quarterly noise.

sections.title: Plants and US FDA status: a Warning Letter (Nacharam formulations) and a Form 483 (Pashamylaram CDMO) in one year; Jaggaiahpet clean

blocks.p: ~3,000+ kL of pilot and commercial capacity: CDMO at Suryapet, Pashamylaram, Vizag (ADC/high potency), Nacharam (oligo); API at Atchutapuram, Jaggaiahpet, Ankleshwar, Jadcherla, Patancheru; specialty chemicals at Genome Valley and Vizag; formulations at Nacharam; NJ Bio at Princeton, New Jersey. In FY26 the network had 12 regulatory audits and 143 customer audits; 11 regulatory audits were closed. Two US FDA issues are open at 30-Sep-2026: the Nacharam Warning Letter and a Form 483 with five observations (none on data integrity) after an inspection of the Pashamylaram CDMO site from 27-Jul to 5-Aug-2026. Customer audits of CDMO and API sites in Q1FY27 had no critical findings.

sections.title: Competitive advantage: real chemistry and innovator relationships, but narrow; the new platforms and the quality record have not earned a moat

blocks.p: A moat is an advantage that lets a company earn more than its cost of capital for longer than rivals. Cohance has two real ones. First, relationships: once an intermediate or API is in an innovator's approved process, switching takes years, and Suven had 30-year relationships with large drug companies. Second, chemistry and cost in niche APIs (controlled substances, CNS molecules, top-three global shares). Against that: the relationships did not widen for years, two big molecules destocked at once, the ADC and oligonucleotide platforms are small or loss-making, and the regulatory record took two hits in 2026. The new chairman's own words: Cohance "is getting onto that path" that Divi's and Laurus took years to build.

sections.title: Two businesses glued together in FY25, then a fall: revenue −13% in FY26 and −23% in Q1FY27; EPS ₹12.68 (FY25, merged) → ₹4.68 → a Q1 loss

blocks.p: Read the history in two parts. **FY20-FY24 is Suven Pharmaceuticals alone**: a pure contract manufacturer for innovator drug companies with revenue of ₹834-1,340 cr and EBITDA margins of 39-46%, the best in Indian pharma. **FY25 onward is the merged company**: Cohance Lifesciences (Advent's API and CDMO platform) was folded in from 1-May-2025 by pooling of interests, so FY25 was restated as if the two had always been one (revenue ₹2,608 cr, of which Suven as first reported was ₹1,198 cr). The +148% jump from FY24 to FY25 is the merger, not growth. Since then the business has shrunk: FY26 revenue fell 13% to ₹2,269 cr as two large CDMO molecules were destocked by their customers (~₹260 cr), API+ fell 8% (a US FDA Warning Letter at the Nacharam formulations plant cost ~₹61 cr) and specialty chemicals slipped 2%. The EBITDA margin halved from 30.6% to 18.8% because the cost base kept rising (new leaders, sales teams, NJ Bio in the US) while revenue fell. We therefore value on **P/E on Sep-28E EPS (half FY28E, half FY29E)**, with EV/EBITDA and a DCF as cross-checks. Our EPS is attributable to owners (after minorities), with no exceptional items.

blocks.h: The structural break, and why the post-merger window cannot set the multiple

blocks.p: Suven Pharmaceuticals absorbed Cohance Lifesciences on **1-May-2025** (11 Suven shares for every 295 Cohance shares; 25.46 cr → 38.26 cr shares), which changed the business and the share count. Following PLAYBOOK §7c, we first started the own one-year-forward median at the effective date (1-May-2025, itself the first day of a month) on a consistent post-merger per-share basis (FY25 restated EPS ₹12.68 on 38.37 cr shares; amortisation of acquired intangibles is small and in both history and forecasts). That window has only two forward years: **FY27E** (for dates May-2025 to Mar-2026) and **FY28E** (Apr-Sep 2026). **Both are trough years** under §4: forward EPS below half the highest EPS of the previous three years. FY25 EPS before exceptional items was ₹13.11, so the line is ₹6.56; our FY27E is ₹3.24 and FY28E ₹5.88 (on reported EPS the line is ₹6.34; same result). Every post-merger point is a trough point: the window's median is 131.4x (FY28E points alone 74.8x), a multiple of depressed earnings that the trough rule exists to exclude. The post-merger window therefore gives no usable median.

The rule leaves the history of the listed share. We use its one-year-forward P/E **since 1-Apr-2021** on every weekly close plus the 30-Sep-2026 close, on the same per-share basis, with trough years FY26, FY27, FY28 left out: the remaining 157 points are the FY23, FY24 and FY25 forward years (Apr-2021 to Mar-2024; Suven alone for FY23-24, the merged FY25 for dates in FY24). This is the since-2021 median the brief asked us to show as a sensitivity; with the post-merger window empty it becomes the base. Exceptional items were material in FY22, FY24 and FY25-26 (Suven gains of ~₹50 cr and ~₹33 cr after tax; merged charges of ₹15.8 cr and ₹29.5 cr), so the base uses EPS before them (batch practice A18); the reported-EPS median (38.4x) is a sensitivity. blocks.callout: **What you are buying:** a niche-API franchise with top-three global positions (API+, ~half of revenue), innovator CDMO relationships with a Phase III pipeline and a restocking order, a fast-growing oligonucleotide building-block business (Sapala), net cash on the company's definition (₹251 cr at Jun-2026) and Umang Vohra. **What you are also buying:** a loss-making US ADC business (NJ Bio) with a put option on the rest, ₹696 cr owed to minority partners, a Warning Letter and a Form 483, a cost base built for a bigger company, and an owner whose shares are 94.6% pledged.

FY27 -1.9%: Q1FY27 revenue fell 23% to Rs422 cr; management guides Q2 better than Q1, year-on-year comparability by end-H1 and growth only in H2 (Q2 'stable', CDMO deliveries moved from Q1 into Q2, a restocking order for Q4FY27-FY28). Our FY27 needs Rs1,803 cr from Q2-Q4, +5% on Rs1,719 cr a year earlier. FY28 +16.0%: restocking of one destocked molecule (order spread over two years) and two newly commercial molecules (six intermediates) lift small-molecule CDMO 25%; API+ and Specialty Chemicals guided to double-digit growth from FY28. FY29 +12.8%. Street FY27E: BOBCAPS Rs2,250 cr; S&P consensus Rs2,260 cr (Rs2,120-2,450 cr); FY28E BOBCAPS Rs2,491 cr.

FY28 Rs740 cr (+25%) on restocking over two years and two more commercial molecules in 12-15 months; FY29 Rs850 cr, still below FY25's ~Rs1,024 cr. NJ Bio Rs150/175/210 cr: Q1FY27 Rs35 cr with 'FTE contract risk this year'; the US facility expansion supports FY28. Sapala Rs100/125/150 cr: Q1FY27 Rs27.4 cr (2.5x) with 'confirmed orders in hand'. Specialty Chemicals -9/12/12%: Q1 -35%, FY27 a qualification year weighted to H2, double-digit growth from FY28.

methods.why: How the street values Cohance: BOBCAPS, the one broker whose method we could read, uses P/E (40x Jun-28E EPS); the CDMO peers are valued on P/E. Structural break: Suven Pharmaceuticals absorbed Cohance Lifesciences from 1-May-2025 (11 Suven shares for 295 Cohance shares; 25.46 cr to 38.26 cr shares). The own window from that date holds two forward years, FY27E (Rs3.24) and FY28E (Rs5.88), and both are trough years (below half of FY25's Rs13.11 before exceptional items, i.e. Rs6.56), so the post-merger window gives no usable median (all points 131.4x; FY28E points 74.8x). 43.5x = the median one-year-forward P/E of the listed share since 1-Apr-2021 on every weekly close plus the 30-Sep close (post-merger per-share basis: FY25 restated EPS on 38.37 cr shares; FY23-24 Suven), on EPS before exceptional items, trough years FY26-FY28 left out (157 points from the FY23-FY25 forward years), of 40.4x x 1.082 (the nine pharma peers' trailing P/E at the 30-Sep close vs their five-year medians, the house factor for names outside the set; reproduced +8.2%) = 43.7x, nearest half-turn. Reported-EPS median 38.4x (sensitivity). Bull 49.5x / bear 37x = 75th / 25th percentile (45.9x / 34.3x) x 1.082. No own-move blend, no growth uplift (sensitivities only). Written by COHANCE.mult.js.

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.why: Cross-check: median one-year-forward EV/EBITDA on the same dates (EV = price x shares then outstanding less the last published net cash; Suven for the FY23-24 forward years, merged pro forma for FY25) of 25.2x x 1.075 (the nine peers' EV/EBITDA move against five-year medians; reproduced +7.5%) = 27.1x, nearest half-turn, on Sep-28E EBITDA plus Sep-28E net cash after the Rs696 cr minority buy-out liability. Bull 31x / bear 24x = 75th / 25th percentile x 1.075.

methods.name: DCF
methods.why: Tests whether cash flows support the price: 15-year FCFF at 12.8% (cost of equity; net debt incl. the minority buy-out liability is small against market value), terminal growth 5.5%, less net debt at Mar-27E including the Rs696 cr minority buy-out liability and leases, plus the Rs260 cr Raisin investment.
